business: Eat Out Better, an iPhone app that rates every dish on a restaurant menu for high cholesterol
target: US adults 40 to 70 told by a clinician their cholesterol or LDL is high (many on a statin), who eat at restaurants or order takeaway at least twice a week and use an iPhone
where: United States, mostly suburban and mid-size cities

segments.name: Newly diagnosed, motivated (told in the last year)
Caregiver or spouse ordering for a partner

behaviours.name: Asks ChatGPT or Googles it
behaviours.how: Already photographs things and asks an AI assistant; sees no reason to pay for a narrower app.

behaviours.name: Rule-of-thumb orderer
behaviours.how: Orders grilled fish or a salad on autopilot and thinks they already know what to pick.

behaviours.name: Tracker
behaviours.how: Logs food in MyFitnessPal or similar and likes numbers.

behaviours.name: Subscription-averse
behaviours.how: Cancels app subscriptions on principle and hates trials that auto-renew.

behaviours.name: Doctor-led
behaviours.how: Does what the cardiologist or dietitian recommends, ignores ads.

behaviours.name: Social eater
behaviours.how: Eats out with friends or clients and won't pull out a phone to scan a menu at the table.

objections: I can just ask ChatGPT for free
I already know to order grilled and skip the fries
How accurate is an AI guess about how a restaurant cooks?
Another subscription for something I use twice a month?
I'm not going to scan the menu in front of people
Is this advice from an actual doctor or dietitian?
My statin handles it, I don't stress about restaurants
habits: you eat lunch out with coworkers twice a week
you get takeaway on Friday nights
you travel for work a few days a month
your doctor told you at your last checkup to cut saturated fat
you eat out with your spouse on weekends
you mostly eat at chains like Chili's, Olive Garden and Panera
